engagement: University of Iowa RFQ 18649 — AIS assessment (preparation only; not an awarded engagement)
note: Components are named by their real lane directory name under revenue/. A component listed here that is not present on disk is reported MISSING, not skipped. A lane present on disk but absent from this manifest is reported UNMAPPED, not dropped. A component may declare a `runner`: its documented command line. A runner is only consulted when the component ships no unittest file, and the status reason always states that the evidence came from the runner rather than from a test suite.

phases.title: Kickoff and mobilization
phases.purpose: Stand the engagement up: scope confirmation, contacts, schedule shape, coordination forms, and the assessment context the whole kit is built against.
operator_does: Read the mobilization plan and hold the scope-confirmation conversation with the University sponsor.
Fill the coordination forms with real named contacts (all currently UNKNOWN).
Record the agreed kickoff date; every date in the kit is relative to it.

components.role: This handoff: the six-phase guide, the component verifier, and the UNKNOWN register. Start here.

runner.note: deterministic self-demo on the synthetic fixture; the lane also ships test_verify_kit.py which the verifier runs in preference to this

components.role: Eight-week and six-week plan shapes, coordination forms, scope-confirmation agenda.
Carrier record and evidence-authority boundary for the whole workstream.
Assessment context notes used to brief the team.

phases.title: Evidence collection
phases.purpose: Gather what the University actually supplies, register it with stable IDs and exact locators, and rehearse the intake path before real documents arrive.
operator_does: Run the intake rehearsal against the synthetic corpus first, so malformed input handling is observed, not assumed.
Register each supplied artifact with a stable evidence ID and an exact locator.
Use the per-area interview worksheets to collect evidence for each assessment area.
Anything not supplied stays UNKNOWN in the register. Never enter a zero for an absent input.

components.role: Fictional AIS evidence corpus; the safe input for every rehearsal.
Intake-to-assessment rehearsal; malformed-input handling.
Locator-preserving extraction from PDF/DOCX/text evidence.
Test-data catalog readiness evidence.
Secure-development guidance usability evidence.
Security-event review and ownership evidence.
Observability and service-objective evidence.
Backup completion vs demonstrated restoration.
Incident timelines, postmortems, corrective-action follow-through.
Deployment record traced to artifact digest and approval evidence.
Development-to-operations handoff packet evidence.
Current AI use: active vs informal experiment vs planned.
AI knowledge and data readiness evidence.

phases.title: Analysis
phases.purpose: Turn registered evidence into findings and prioritized recommendations with visible weights and explicit units.
operator_does: Apply the rating model to each assessment area using only supplied evidence.
Run the prioritization calculator; inspect the sensitivity output before accepting an order.
Keep every finding pointed at the evidence ID it came from — the traceability rehearsal is the check.

components.role: Area rating with an explicit decision table.
Recommendation prioritization with visible weights and sensitivity.
Delivery metric calculation, data dictionary, interpretation notes.
Adoption vs operational outcome, kept separate.
Local analyst surface over the workshare compiler.
Workflow capacity benchmark; measured vs estimated.
AI task suitability, benefit, integration effort.
Policy-to-workflow assessment (NIST AI RMF as reference only).
Organizational adoption readiness; never rates individuals.
Integration and portability readiness patterns.
AI usefulness evaluation tasks with known answers.

phases.title: Draft review
phases.purpose: Prove the draft is followable back to source and usable by its readers, and capture feedback without flattening disagreement.
operator_does: Run the traceability validator; a broken trace is a blocker, not a footnote.
Run the documentation usability method against the draft with a real reviewer task.
Record unresolved disagreements as unresolved. Do not resolve them by deletion.

components.role: Evidence to finding to recommendation to report-line trace validator.

runner.note: validates the synthetic evidence->finding->recommendation->report-line trace bundle shipped in the lane

components.role: Reviewer usability method and worksheets.
Evidence-backed discussion and Q&A kit.
CSV/JSON/doc interchange verification for review handoffs.

phases.title: Final delivery
phases.purpose: Assemble the RFQ-aligned final report, check its accessible visual language, and close the evidence lifecycle.
operator_does: Assemble the report against the RFQ-aligned structure.
Check the visual language reads without color alone and that unassessed cells stay visibly distinct from assessed ones.
Run the closeout validator. It validates disposition records; it deletes nothing.

components.role: RFQ-aligned final-report structure.
Accessible visual language; unassessed stays distinct.
Field-name and taxonomy reconciliation across components.

runner.note: reconciles field names across component CSV/JSON outputs; --repo takes the repository root (the parent of the survey root), which is what its interface map's relative paths are written against

components.role: Evidence lifecycle and 30-day post-completion closeout templates.

phases.title: Optional readout
phases.purpose: Optional leadership readout. The deck must agree with the delivered report; detail lives in the appendix.
operator_does: Build the deck from the delivered report, not from a parallel narrative.
Rehearse Q&A only against evidence that is actually in the report.

components.role: Deck architecture that agrees with the example report.
Q&A answers substantiated from supplied evidence.
